A theme for Da Librarby

Snowdin

Cozy and warm, at night in a little snowy town underground: soft snow drifting past, string lights on the trees, warm light from the windows, a crackling fire inside. The game's black-and-white text boxes and the little red heart are the frame, with normal words where they matter and game-style flavor around them.

This is a plan and a mockup, not the real app yet. Point at things, try the switches below, and tell me what you'd change.

Sounds start after your first click on the page (browsers require that). In the app, these would be options in Settings while Snowdin is chosen.

♥The look

Night-blue instead of pure black, so it feels like a quiet evening rather than a battle. Warm amber and ember light, snowy white, pine green and wood. Yellow is kept for one job, like in the game: it shows what you're pointing at.

Fonts

A pixel font for titles, buttons, menus and numbers. For longer text (descriptions), you can compare the pixel font with a smooth, rounded one using the "Long text" switch above. Both fonts are free to include in the project.

♥Home

The app's name on a snowy wooden town sign. The artwork above becomes its sky. Its description is a text box that types itself out (click it to finish at once). Continue watching becomes save files with the twinkling save star. ♥The plan

The theme system grows

Today a theme can only change colours, fonts and shapes. Snowdin needs a few new abilities. They'll be built so the other four themes stay exactly as they are, and future themes can use them too:

  • Decorations: a theme can add things like the snow, string lights and trees.
  • A pointer: a theme can show something (the heart) next to whatever you point at or pick with the keyboard.
  • Its own words: a theme can replace texts like empty-page messages, loading lines and flavor text.
  • Typing text: descriptions and messages can type themselves out.
  • Sounds: a theme can bring its own sounds.
  • Its own icons (pixel ones here) and its own settings (snow, sounds, typing, long-text font).

Building it, in stages

After each stage you get screenshots and can try it in the app.

1Foundation

  • The new theme abilities above
  • Colours, fonts, pixel art (heart, save star, snow caps, the town and forest, sign, dog)
  • Snowdin appears in Settings with its preview

2Library screens

  • Town sign, navigation, search
  • Spotlight with the town or forest, lights and snow
  • Save-file cards, covers, rows, "NEW!"
  • Right-click menus, messages, empty and loading screens

3Show pages

  • Battle-screen layout, text box, buttons
  • Season tabs, episode rows
  • The "Fix match" window

4Settings

  • Boxes and switches in the game's style
  • Snowdin's own options
  • Its card in Appearance

5Player

  • HP-bar seek bar with the heart
  • Text-box menus and next-episode card
  • Mini player frame

6Sounds, Easter eggs, polish

  • All the sounds, tuned quiet
  • Easter eggs (below)
  • A last check of every screen, and that the other themes are unchanged

Easter eggs (secret until you find them in the app)

  • Something happens when you search for a certain very determined word.
  • The town sign has something to say about its spelling if you click it.
  • Late at night, a certain motherly goat has opinions about your bedtime.
  • In December, the town gets more festive.
  • The little dog shows up where you don't expect it, very rarely.

Keeping it comfy

  • Snow is slow and sparse, and stays behind text. Nothing flashes.
  • Typing text is quick, a click finishes it, and it only types the first time you see something.
  • If Windows is set to reduce animations, the snow and typing stop on their own.
  • Everything stays easy to read: if pixel text tires your eyes, long text can switch to the smooth font.

About copyright

Everything in this theme (pixel art, sounds, wording, fonts) would be made by me or freely licensed, so it can be on GitHub. Nothing is taken from the game's files. The flavor lines are written in the game's style, with a couple of famous short phrases like "But nobody came."

Questions for you

  • Pixel or smooth font for long text?
  • Should the heart, the snow caps on covers, and the string lights all be there, or is anything too much?
  • Navigation at the top (as shown), or a sidebar like in Neon, perhaps as a wooden bookshelf?
  • Do the sounds feel right? Louder, softer, fewer?
